When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) consulted with the Sahabah (RA) about whom to send to Bahrain, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) said, "Send the person whom Rasulullaah ﷺ had sent to them (the people of Bahrain), the one who made them Muslims and subservient. Someone whom they will recognise, who recognises them and who knows their land." Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) was referring to Hadhrat Alaa bin Hadhrami (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) however, refused to accept the proposal and said, "Force Abaan bin Sa'eed bin Al Aas to return because he is a man who has been there several times." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) refused to force him saying, "I shall not do it. I cannot force a person who says that he will not accept a post of command from anyone after Rasulullaah ﷺ." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then confirmed that Hadhrat Alaa bin Hadhrami (RA) would be sent to Bahrain. [^1]
Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) Refuses to Accept an Appointment as Ameer

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once summoned him to accept a post as governor, but he refused to accept the post. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "You dislike an appointment to a post when someone better than you actually asked for it." When Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) asked who it was that asked for a post, Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "Yusuf bin Ya'qoob (AS)." Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) then said, "Yusuf (AS) was the Nabi of Allaah and the son of a Nabi, while I am merely Abu Hurayrah the son of Umayma. I fear three and two things (equalling five)." "Why don't you just say 'five things'?" enquired Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) replied, "I fear that I should say anything without knowledge, pass wrong judgement (as a governor, because of which I would) have my back lashed, have my wealth taken away and my reputation insulted." [^2]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) Refuses to be Appointed as judge

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mowhab reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), "Go and pass judgement between the people." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) requested, "Will you not excuse me, O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) emphatically said, "Never! I have sworn that you must be the judge."
